summary: Redwood AE + SE demo of rate limiting, quota controls, and org/project keys for HealthCentral multi-tenant setup. Focus on per-project quotas, per-route rate limits, token scoping, billing separation, and security controls (SSO, KMS). Customer asked about dedicated vs hosted, burst capacity and audit logs. Agreed next steps: pricing, sample policy, and traffic estimates.
transcript:
Header:
Date: 2025-07-10
Start: 16:00 PDT
Duration: ~45 minutes
Attendees: Jordan (Redwood AE), Priya (Redwood SE), Evan (Redwood Solutions), Mark (HealthCentral CTO), Sophie (Eng Mgr), Ravi (Security), Anita (DevOps)

[00:00] Jordan: okay everyone, thanks for joining, can you hear me okay?
[00:03] Mark: yeah loud and clear, thanks.
[00:05] Jordan: awesome, quick agenda — we'll walk the Console demo for org and project keys, show rate limiting and quotas, then Priya will do a quick Optimize-run tradeoffs for batching and burst capacity; then we'll leave time for Q&A.
[00:18] Sophie: sounds good. just so you know our main concern is multi-tenant billing separation and per-tenant rate limits.
[00:25] Jordan: totally, that's exactly what we'll focus on.
[00:28] Priya: hi all, i'll start with the console — please bear with a little screen lag — i'll show how we create an org, then projects, then generate scoped keys, and attach per-project quotas.
[00:40] [screen share starts - console UI noises]
[00:45] Priya: here is the org-level page, you can see global settings, billing owner, SSO config, and a keys tab. we'll create a new project called "hc-telemetry" and then you can set a project quota here: token quota per month, requests per minute, and a route-level rate limit override.
[01:10] Anita: can you set different billing accounts per project? we run multiple BU's with separate POs.
[01:15] Priya: yes — you can attach a billing account to a project or inherit from org. billing separation is supported; invoice will show project tags. it's also possible to emit per-project usage to your billing export S3.
[01:28] Ravi: how granular are these rate limits? per API key? per IP? per org?
[01:33] Priya: we support multiple dimensions — per-key, per-project, per-org, and route-level. the typical pattern for multi-tenant SaaS is: issue project-scoped keys to tenant apps (so limits are enforced per-tenant) and then use org-wide fallback policies.
[01:48] Mark: and if a tenant spikes, can we configure a burst policy? like keep them above baseline for short windows?
[01:55] Priya: yes, we have burst capacity and token-bucket style burst windows. you can configure steady-rate and burst capacity; there are also priority tiers if you want certain projects to have guaranteed throughput.
[02:07] Jordan: to add, Dedicated customers can reserve capacity for predictable throughput — if you need guaranteed low latency at high QPS for a tenant we usually recommend dedicated pools or a guaranteed bandwidth policy.
[02:18] Sophie: quick Q on scoped keys — do they rotate automatically and can they be scoped to specific routes like embeddings-only vs generation?
[02:24] Priya: keys can be scoped to scopes like embeddings-only, generation-only, or custom routes. rotation can be automated via API; you can also mint short-lived keys from a service account.
[02:38] [slight crosstalk]
[02:40] Ravi: security — we need audit logs and KMS. can we send logs to our Splunk and use our KMS for key encryption?
[02:46] Priya: yes, audit logs are available — we stream logs to customer endpoints or S3; Splunk is common. and we integrate with external KMS/HSM for private deployments; for hosted we support customer-managed keys via our KMS integrations.
[02:58] Mark: what about SOC 2 / ISO stuff? we're in healthcare and need paper trails.
[03:03] Jordan: we have SOC 2 and are pursuing ISO; i'll attach our compliance pack. also the private deployment option gives you a private control plane and full auditability.
[03:14] Sophie: great. can you show how rate limiting looks in a high-traffic scenario — like a fuzzy simulation?
[03:21] Priya: i'll switch to the "traffic simulator" in the Console — note simulator is for demo only, real metrics come from our telemetry.
[03:30] [simulated traffic noise]
[03:32] Priya: injecting a 500 RPS spike against a single project — you can see per-key throttle events come up, and the baseline bucket protects org-level throughput. here's an example where tenant A hits its per-project QPS and we return 429s for that key while other tenants are unaffected.
[03:53] Anita: okay that's helpful — do 429s include a Retry-After with recommended backoff? we need graceful clients.
[03:59] Priya: yes, we return standard Retry-After headers and include the throttle reason in the response body; you can also configure a soft-limit that returns warnings in telemetry without 429s.
[04:12] Mark: how easy is it to add a new project programmatically? we spin up new tenants frequently.
[04:18] Priya: there's full REST and SDK support — in the demo i can create a project via CLI, mint a scoped key, and attach a quota in under a minute.
[04:27] [Priya types, CLI output appears]
[04:30] Priya: example CLI: redwood projects create --org hc --name tenant-123 --quota 1M-tokens --billing-account bc-102 
[04:40] Sophie: good. another question — we do a lot of embeddings; can we set separate token quotas per-model or per-route? embeddings behave differently cost-wise.
[04:48] Priya: yes, route-level quotas let you set different budgets for embeddings vs generation. Optimize will also suggest quantization and batching profiles to lower cost for embeddings-heavy workloads.
[04:59] Jordan: and our Optimize tool can run on sample traffic to recommend batching windows and cache prefixes — that usually reduces token cost 20-50% depending on prefix reuse.
[05:12] Mark: earlier you mentioned KV cache — how does that impact rate limiting? if we have a hot cache, we still count tokens?
[05:20] Priya: good question — KV cache reduces compute but we still meter tokens for billing, though cache hits can reduce latency and cost footprint. note some internal terms sometimes get mis-transcribed in call notes — kv cache might show up as K V cache or K-V in the transcript.
[05:34] Ravi: any rate-limit configs that are tenant-aware in Dedicated vs hosted? differences?
[05:39] Priya: functionally similar controls, but Dedicated gives you isolated pools so noisy-neighbor risk is lower and you can set stricter SLA-backed throughput. Hosted has shared pools but supports strong per-project policies and burst allowances.
[05:54] Sophie: what about enforcement for long-running streaming requests? like open-ended chat sessions that hold connections.
[06:01] Priya: streaming sessions are tracked for concurrent connection limits; there are per-project concurrent-stream caps and per-token throttles — if you hit the concurrent limit we return a 429-like connection-reject.
[06:14] Mark: okay, let's talk about rollout — if we enable per-tenant keys, we need a migration path from our existing single-key plan.
[06:21] Jordan: typical rollout: start with issuing project-scoped keys to a subset of tenants, monitor via per-key telemetry, then gradually move more tenants, using canary policies. Console supports A/B policies and percent rollouts.
[06:33] Anita: can we have policy inheritance? e.g., set org default, then override for individual projects?
[06:38] Priya: yes, hierarchical policies: org default -> project override -> key-specific override. precedence is explicit in the UI.
[06:45] [brief pause]
[06:47] Mark: pricing — if we set per-project quotas, is billing prorated? we prefer predictable monthly line items.
[06:53] Jordan: invoices can show per-project usage and you can set monthly committed-use discounts for Dedicated. Hosted invoices are usage-based but you can set monthly budget alerts and soft quotas.
[07:05] Sophie: any gotchas with SSO or SCIM when provisioning projects? we want automated onboarding.
[07:10] Priya: SCIM provisioning for users is supported; projects currently must be created via API/CLI but you can integrate it in your onboarding pipeline.
[07:20] Ravi: about logs — can we get per-tenant request bodies in logs for debugging? we have PHI constraints so we may not want full payloads stored.
[07:27] Priya: we mask or redact sensitive fields and you can configure log retention and redaction rules. for PHI-sensitive workloads we recommend Private deployment so logs stay in your VPC and you control retention.
[07:40] Mark: ok good. now can you show the rate-limit policy JSON or export? we want to embed it into our infra repo.
[07:46] Priya: sure, exporting policy is possible — i'll show a sample policy JSON quickly. note this is demo-only, but structure is something like: {"policy":"type:token_bucket", "limits":[{"scope":"project","rps":50,"burst":100}]} — transcript may mangle quotes.
[08:08] [small laughter at transcription quirks]
[08:12] Jordan: quick objection we hear from customers — complexity of managing lots of keys. how do you all feel about that?
[08:18] Mark: we already have internal secrets manager; as long as keys can be rotated and minted by automation it's fine.
[08:24] Sophie: rotation is important, also ability to mint ephemeral keys for mobile clients.
[08:28] Priya: yep, ephemeral keys via service accounts are supported; best practice is to mint short-lived tokens in your backend and avoid shipping long-lived keys to clients.
[08:36] Anita: performance — if we put per-tenant limits, will we see increased latency for the limit checks?
[08:42] Priya: checks are done in the control plane but are optimized — typical added latency is a few ms; with caching and local enforcement checks it's negligible for most apps. if you need ultra-low latency you'd look at edge-enforced policies or Dedicated pools.
[08:57] Mark: can you reiterate about fallback policies if capacity is constrained? e.g., fallback to cheaper model or lower-precision quantized variant?
[09:05] Priya: yes, routing policies let you fallback to compatible model variants or lower-cost quantized models. you can configure auto-fallbacks by latency/cost thresholds. Optimize can suggest which model variants to fallback to based on your workload profile.
[09:20] Jordan: wrapping up, what are the main blockers for you to start a pilot?
[09:25] Mark: security signoff and network setup, plus we need an estimated cost model.
[09:29] Sophie: timeline — we want a 6-week POC if costs look reasonable.
[09:33] Jordan: great — we'll send pricing + POC plan. Priya, anything to add?
[09:37] Priya: i'll include sample policy JSON, console walkthrough recording, and an Optimize sample run on synthetic traffic to show typical savings.
[09:45] Ravi: thanks, also send our Security questionnaire answers/space for you to fill.
[09:49] Jordan: noted. next steps recap in the doc we'll send. thanks everyone.

End of transcript.
